questions.explain: An MCP server exposes tools (callable functions wrapping stored procedures), resources (allowlisted readable schema/data), and prompts (analytical templates) over one uniform protocol.
options: Tools (procedures), resources (allowlisted schemas), and prompts (templates) over a uniform protocol
questions.q: What does an MCP server expose over SQL Server?

questions.explain: Tools wrap stored procedures — never raw SQL; the resource allowlist is explicit (schema discovery ≠ schema exposure); session context is stamped per MCP session from the authenticated caller.
options: Tools wrap stored procedures never raw SQL; explicit resource allowlist; per-session context stamping
Allow raw SQL tools for power users
questions.q: What are the three load-bearing design decisions of the MCP server?

questions.explain: Generate against the allowlisted schema, validate before execution (single SELECT only, allowlisted tables, enforced TOP), then execute as the least-privilege login with RLS active as the final backstop.
options: Let the model run any SQL it generates
Generate → validate (SELECT-only, allowlisted tables, enforced TOP) → execute as least-privilege login with RLS
Validation is unnecessary with a good model
questions.q: How is text-to-SQL executed safely through MCP?

questions.explain: Four layers: authenticated MCP transport mapped to tenant/user, least-privilege SQL logins (mcp_reader gets EXECUTE on whitelisted procedures only), RLS on every table, and complete audit logging of every tool call.
options: A shared SQL login for all MCP clients
Authenticated transport + least-privilege logins + RLS on every table + full audit logging
questions.q: What is the layered MCP security model?

questions.explain: Operate MCP like an API: per-client rate limits, versioned tool contracts (deprecate don't mutate), anomaly monitoring on call patterns, and the adversarial suite extended to the MCP surface.
options: Rate limits, versioned contracts, anomaly monitoring, adversarial tests extended to MCP
